newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to clear BA buy of Air Liberte.
newsitem.headline: EU to clear BA buy of Air Liberte.

text.p: The European Commission is set to clear British Airways Plc's takeover of French insolvent airline Air Liberte, the spokesman for Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said confirming a hint by Van Miert himself on Tuesday.

Van Miert told a meeting of the European Parliament's transport committee that BA's chairman Robert Ayling had come to Brussels recently "to thank (the Commission) for its intervention in the Air Liberte case". He added that the French government had tried to pull out a few tricks, but did not elaborate.
Van Miert's spokesman told Reuters on Wednesday his comments meant the acquisition would be cleared.
Van Miert was at the parliament to brief on the controversial alliance between British Airways and AMR's American Airlines.
BA submitted its proposed takeover of Air Liberte to the Commission for clearance under the EU's merger rules on January 29. The Commission has until next week to take a decision.
Air Liberte went into receivership in September and BA, which already owns French carrier TAT, put in a bid for it.

Industry and legal sources said the French government tried to counter the bid by having ailing regional airline AOM, which is owned by French state-controlled bank Credit Lyonnais, to put in a rival proposal.
AOM never formally proposed to buy Air Liberte.

The sources said the French government backtracked after the Commission intervened to point out that it would not look with a keen eye at the acquisition by AOM, because of its relationship with Lyonnais which has been receiving huge subsidies since 1994.
AOM itself is part of a vast group of loss-making assets hived off from the Lyonnais in 1996 to help it survive a reckless expansion in the late 80s. The divested assets are expected to be sold off.

"It was argued with the Commission that AOM should not buy any companies," a source said, adding that this would almost be the equivalent of allowing subsidies given to Lyonnais to carry the purchase. -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
